terms.meaning: named values, such as keys and addresses, that the program reads when it starts

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loads settings and prints lengths
sections.what: Loads the environment settings from the project folder and prints the database address along with the length of each key.
sections.why: Prints lengths instead of key text, so the check is safe to share.

summary: Loads the Next.js environment settings and prints the database address and the length of each key.
purpose: Helps confirm the settings are being read without showing the keys themselves.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: a safer version of the diagnostic script that shows only key lengths.
how: Load the environment settings from the project folder. Print the database address. Print the length of the public key and the service key.
inputs: The environment settings in the project folder.
outputs: Three printed lines to the terminal.
risks: Low risk. The database address is public, and key lengths reveal nothing useful.
debug: If lengths show as 0, the environment file is missing or the variable names differ.
